---
title: "The Story: Shapes of the Game"
---

## Physical Archetypes in Baseball

Baseball has always been a game of specialized roles. Unlike sports where athletes converge on a single ideal body type, baseball demands vastly different physical profiles depending on what each position requires on the field.

When we inspect height and weight across positions, distinct physical archetypes immediately stand out:

- **Pitchers** dominate the upper bounds of height, using longer levers and arm extension to generate velocity and steep release angles towards home plate.
- **Catchers and First Basemen** carry greater mass relative to their height, providing durability behind the plate and power at the corners.
- **Middle Infielders (Second Basemen and Shortstops)** cluster tightly in the lower-left corner of height and weight distributions, prioritizing agility, quick lateral acceleration, and swift transfer times over raw size.

Looking at these physical groupings reveals how role specialization shapes the roster of modern Major League Baseball.
